setup: (fset 'my-when (if (fboundp 'defmacro) (cons 'macro (lambda (c b) (list 'if c b))) (macro (c b) (list 'if c b))))
note: 10B: the fixpoint walks both `defalias` links and then applies the transformer, reaching `(not 7)`. The setup is dialect-neutral by construction: Emacs stores a macro as a `(macro . FUNCTION)` cons in the function cell and fe has a distinct macro object, so each transformer is installed through whichever spelling the running dialect has, selected by `(fboundp 'defmacro)` -- t in Emacs, nil in standalone fe. Nothing else about the case differs between the sides. The transformers deliberately expand to forms both dialects spell identically (`if`, `+`, `not`): fe's implicit body is `do` where Emacs' is `progn`, and fe prints `(quote x)` where Emacs prints `'x`, and neither of those is what these cases are about.
